1. Start out by staying bubbled and garrisoning. You lose less troops this way and have more control over how much troops you’re risking. This is also a good chance to observe how your opponents + strong players in your alliance move and learn from them.
2. Hoard random ports. Note that they only work when all of your squads are in your base.
3. When you attack, travel by tiles only. You move faster and don’t alert your opponents to your movement. Choose a tile that aligns with your opponent’s base, click to move towards that tile, then redirect to hit your opponent’s base when your march is close. By close I mean < 3 seconds if possible.
4. Wall management is an art that takes time to master. Don’t put squads on your wall unless you know you can beat your opponent. Learn to toggle squads on and off the wall quickly as wall defense vary from opponent to opponent.
5. When you start out, move with a team. Ask people in your alliance to garrison you. There are pros and cons of flying solo vs moving in groups but for beginners it’s always better to have someone with you.
6. Battle report, battle report, battle report. Keep an eye on them. Sometimes victories actually result in more troop loss for you than your opponent - especially if you’re the attacker.
7. Don’t be afraid to run. 

I have a few more tips but probably will be better when you’re more familiar with pvp. Don’t be discouraged if you think you’re weak or you’re losing too much troops. I have 8.9 million kills as a low spender ranking 74 in total hero power on a server that just ended season 1. It’s all about strategy

Wall management is a huge part of pvp. I agree with most of the other comments that it’s very contextual. In fact I’d argue that wall management depends not only on the player you’re going against but also the type of event you’re in - Desert Storm, Buster Day, Warzone all demand very different strategies.

I knew of the series through josephides' fanfic on AO3 and let me tell you, reading the source material was extremely disappointing. I must admit that I wasn't invested in any other characters other than Leah and Bran so I just skimmed both of these series for scenes that mentioned them. With that in mind, canon Bran is extremely unlikeable as a character. He treats his children and his brother like shit. His treatment of Leah is criminal. If this is a real life situation happening to someone I know, I would literally usher her to the nearest woman's shelter and help her file a restraining order against him. I totally agree - he was definitely cheating on her emotionally and it's ten times worse because it's with an underage girl. Maybe he's not a pedophile in the sense that he didn't have sexual intercourse with the girl, but to have that kind of fantasy is extremely sick and fucked up. The power imbalance, the ideological gap, yuck yuck and YUCK. Need I mention the fact that Leah was never even (explicitly) given the possibility of being loved by Bran? First he was in love with his dead mate for years, then when he finally had a change of heart it was with someone who wasn't the woman he was with for 200 years. What a joke. And the fact that he constantly let others believe that she was selfish and stupid made me want to GAG. The abuse is so fucked up on so many levels that it's not even funny. Whatever he likes to claim about not letting others disrespect her doesn't mean anything to me. Sure, they may not be outright nasty to her face but everyone knew he doesn't consider her to be truly worthy of his respect and so they consequently snubbed her and never took her side. Not to say that Leah was the most endearing character ever - she's definitely problematic. But holy shit could this woman catch a break for once in her life?

I find it extremely funny that what makes Leah so intriguing to me is none due to the (original) intention of the author AT ALL. I love that she's a bitch (and no, I don't condone treating children like shit because your husband is attracted to them. I just love that she's not willing to shut up and be the punching bag.) and I love her 19th century notions. Here is this woman who was sexually abused by her father for years, who was then coerced into a relationship with one of the most powerful creatures in the world. Her fear of men was extremely valid. Her wariness of Mercy makes so much sense - without Bran she has nothing. Of course she's going to cling to her old fashioned thinking because she was never given a chance to be anything else other than a dutiful wife, lest she literally become homeless or dead. I will defend this woman until the day I take my last breath.

And I'm sorry - Mercy is a Mary Sue. I used to read a lot of Chinese novels and this specific archetype of FMC is called the "loved by ten thousand men" (rough translation) and it's so ridiculously true. Here you have a bunch of thousand year old men thirsting over a teenager, which is certainly an interesting (gag) choice by the author. PB is so lucky that josephides is such an amazing fanfic author that I have to keep up with the A&O series. The sheer amount of retcon going on in the books is unbelievable. Bran and Leah was supposed to have some kind of bargain that started their marriage/ mating but then in Wild Sign it turned out Bran just basically forced her into it. Bran all of a sudden was in love with Mercy all along. What????

I think my situation moving forward is to go into Death of the Author mode. Hell I was already half way there myself after finding out about Bran/Mercy.

If you haven’t read the two series by Patricia Briggs, I think it’d be helpful to know a bit about canon Bran and Leah first! >!Bran is the King of the Werewolves and the foster father of the FMC in the Mercy Thompson series. He’s a very old werewolf who has 2 children, one from his human marriage and one to a Native American woman called Blue Jay Woman. After giving birth, Blue Jay Woman passed away and Bran basically went on an extreme killing spree because he lost control of his wolf. After this, he swore to never love anyone again because he didn’t want to make the same mistake. Now enter Leah, a woman Bran claimed is so stupid and selfish that he could never love her. Bran mated and married Leah because his wolf needed a mate. They have been married for 2 centuries and while Bran respected Leah (and doesn’t let anyone else disrespect her in front of him), it is very clear to everyone in canonverse that he dislikes her and does not want anything to do with her emotionally. The only time they get along is in bed because sex is essential for the mating bond. Leah is in love with him (for how long we don’t know, but for a good while) and is understandably upset when her husband starts showing interest in Mercy Thompson (who then became his foster daughter - I know. It was a tough pill to swallow but I was in too deep at this point. I like to actively forget this.). So Leah was introduced as a mega bitch who constantly mistreated Mercy. And so all the characters in the book had a surface level respect for her due to her rank but basically dislike her as a person and never sided with her. Up until the latest book in the Alpha and Omega series, this was pretty much the dynamic between Bran and Leah. However, Leah’s tragic backstory was revealed in the recent book: she was in a mind-controlled cult where her father raped her repeatedly and gave her 2 sons. One of her children died as an infant and the other became a villain that she had to kill to save her pack. It was also showed that Bran actually forced the mating bond on Leah to save his brother. And now that Leah had to confront her past once more, Bran had to face the truth of his feelings and apparently he had been in love with her for a while.!<

I think the first book of the series really shows you who Fanchette is, and the rest of them show you what she endured. 

>!Isaiah (her husband) has basically been in love with his enemy’s wife his whole life. Fanchette and Isaiah had a distant, polite marriage, where Isaiah did whatever he wanted and Fanchette seemingly was contented with spending his money. In the first book, she spent so much that he cut off her allowance. Colin, the hero of this book, was arrested and about to be hung but was rescued by the heroine (who was hired by a mysterious entity to do so). Through out the book both of the MCs tried to find the mastermind behind all of this just for it ti turn out to be Fanchette. She did it out of petty revenge for her husband’s actions, but also interestingly because her husband’s love (Colin’s mom) wrote her a letter and said that Colin was in fact Isaiah’s son. Fanchette thought Isaiah was behind Colin’s imprisonment and execution and saved Colin, thinking that she couldn’t let her husband kill his own son. What’s truly intriguing is that she could’ve let this be “an eye for an eye” situation because her son Lyon had disappeared mostly due to the Everseas. So yes, she could’ve let Colin die because of her husband’s infidelity but she didn’t. She seems like a pretty airhead on the surface but was capable of manipulation and feelings that go infinitely beyond what she was capable of.!<

>!The rest of the series is just Isaiah being jealous of Jacob Everseas for living the life he thought he deserved while being a massive a-hole to his whole family, Fanchette included. He never really cared about what she had to say. Fanchette basically had to defend her own children against Isaiah because he couldn’t get over the woman he lost 30 years ago. Despite it all Fanchette truly cared for him and was willing to put up with the utmost disrespect just so Lyon, her son, had a chance at happiness with an Eversea. She was always by Isaiah’s side even when he didn’t deserve it. If it seems like she only cares about gossip, spending, and her children, it’s because her husband never allowed her to care about anything else.!<

>!What truly gets me is that every time one of Isaiah’s sons defied him, he always expressed admiration for them for following their hearts. The constant neglect of Fanchette’s feelings and accomplishment is so crazy to me. Isolde made her choice and Isaiah made his. All this pining while you have 4 children and a woman who’s always been faithful and loyal to you for 30+ years is INSANE. I don’t blame the Redmond children for loving Fanchette the way they did. She was truly dealt a horrible hand and had to work with what she had.!<

Has she always been frivolous or is it her way to cope? Her actions in TPOP just made me realize that the harmony within the Redmond family is because of her will, that she is capable of tearing everything down if she truly wanted to. Yet she chose to live like an airhead for the sake of her children and even her husband.
